$comment: Containers vs virtual machines. Analogy: detached house vs flat in one building. Round 2: fewer sections, buildings shown, bracket + command.

title.text: Containers vs VMs: flats or houses
title.subtitle: Both keep apps apart. They share different things.

sections.label: Analogy: a house and a flat

actors.says: My own boiler. It takes a while to heat.
actors.name: Vera
Block of flats
actors.caption:
one shared boiler,
a locked door per flat

actors.says: Heating is already on. I just walk in.
actors.name: Tom

sections.text: A VM pretends to be a whole computer. A container is an ordinary process, fenced off on the host.

sections.label: VM: a house with its own boiler

layers.name: Guest OS
layers.text: a full OS with its own kernel, e.g. Ubuntu or Windows

layers.name: Hypervisor
layers.text: fakes CPU, RAM and disks for each VM (KVM, Hyper-V, ESXi)

sections.label: Container: a flat in one building

layers.name: Your app
layers.text: your program plus the files it needs, but no kernel

layers.name: Runtime
layers.text: starts and fences the processes (containerd, runc)

layers.name: Host kernel
layers.text: one Linux kernel for all: namespaces = walls, cgroups = meters

rows.a: its own, inside the guest OS
rows.b: the host's Linux kernel, shared by all

rows.a: typically tens of seconds: a whole OS must boot
rows.b: typically under a second: the kernel is already running
typically tens to hundreds of megabytes

rows.a: stronger: a kernel bug usually stays in one VM
rows.b: weaker: a kernel bug can reach every flat

rows.a: a Windows VM can run on a Linux host
rows.b: Linux containers need a Linux kernel

sections.label: Try it: move into a flat

items.note: starts nginx in the background; host port 8080 -> port 80 inside. Pulls the image if missing.
lists running containers: the flats someone lives in
lists images: the floor plans the flats are built from

sections.label: Flats inside a house
sections.text: Docker Desktop runs Linux containers inside a small Linux VM. In the cloud, many containers run inside VMs too.
A VM brings its own kernel, like a house with its own boiler. Containers share the host kernel, like flats share one boiler.
